name.text: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — exact values and the principal range

questiontext.text:
Find the exact value of \( [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin^{-1}[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos^{-1}[[else]]\tan^{-1}[[/if]]\left({@val@}\right) \), giving your answer in radians as a multiple of \(\pi\).

Type \(\pi\) as pi, for example 3*pi/4.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
An inverse trigonometric function must give exactly one output, so it is defined on a restricted principal range:

  • \(\sin^{-1}\) returns a value in \(\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\);
  • \(\cos^{-1}\) returns a value in \(\left[0, \pi\right]\);
  • \(\tan^{-1}\) returns a value in \(\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

We need the angle \(\theta\) in \([[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right][[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\left[0, \pi\right][[else]]\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)[[/if]]\) with \([[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos[[else]]\tan[[/if]]\theta = {@val@}\). The reference angle with \([[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos[[else]]\tan[[/if]]\theta = {@abs(val)@}\) is \({@k*%pi@}\).[[if test="is(val<0)"]] The value is negative, so [[if test="is(fn=1)"]]\(\theta\) lies in the second quadrant: \(\cos^{-1}(-a) = \pi - \cos^{-1}(a)\).[[else]]\(\theta\) is negative: \([[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin^{-1}[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos^{-1}[[else]]\tan^{-1}[[/if]](-a) = -[[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin^{-1}[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos^{-1}[[else]]\tan^{-1}[[/if]](a)\).[[/if]][[/if]] Infinitely many other angles have the same ratio, but only this one lies in the principal range.

So \( [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin^{-1}[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos^{-1}[[else]]\tan^{-1}[[/if]]\left({@val@}\right) = {@ta@} \).

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.10 (Inverse of Trigonometric Functions). Evaluates inverse sine, cosine or tangent at a standard value, including negative inputs; catches an out-of-principal-range angle, an answer in degrees, and sign errors (including the odd-function rule misapplied to inverse cosine). Inverse and forward trig functions are forbidden in the answer so the CAS cannot evaluate it for the student.

input.name: ans1
input.forbidwords: asin, acos, atan, arcsin, arccos, arctan, sin, cos, tan

node.description: Same ratio, outside the principal range

truefeedback.text: That angle does have the right ratio, but it lies outside the principal range \([[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right][[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\left[0, \pi\right][[else]]\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)[[/if]]\), so it is not the value the inverse function returns.
That is the angle in degrees. Give it in radians, as a multiple of \(\pi\): \(180^\circ = \pi\) radians.

Check the sign. [[if test="is(fn=1)"]]\(\cos^{-1}\) only returns angles in \([0, \pi]\), so its value is never negative. For a negative input use \(\cos^{-1}(-a) = \pi - \cos^{-1}(a)\).[[else]]The output of this inverse function has the same sign as its input.[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Find the angle in the principal range \([[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right][[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\left[0, \pi\right][[else]]\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)[[/if]]\) whose [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]sine[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]cosine[[else]]tangent[[/if]] is \({@val@}\). Start from the exact values at \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
